_about: How the certificates lens reads the certificates of a footprint. A certificate is an asset of certificate_types reached from a controlled asset by a relation whose purpose is certificate_purpose (a service presenting it, a name it covers); certificate authority certificates (ca_field true) are skipped. fields names the content fields read. name_types are the assets a certificate covers. A certificate is reported when it has expired or expires within expiry_warning_days, when it was issued by its own subject, when its signature algorithm is one of weak_signature_algorithms (names as Go's crypto/x509 prints them; SHA-1 and MD5 signatures are no longer accepted by browsers), when its validity is longer than max_validity allows for the date it was issued (the CA/Browser Forum's Baseline Requirements cap it, on a schedule), and, for review, when it is a wildcard or covers names of other domains. Add values here, not in Go code.
